chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the child of adultery (bastard): do I buy him, or sell him, or make him serve? He said: Buy him, and enslave him, and make him serve, and sell him. But as for the foundling, do not buy him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying and selling a child of adultery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the juristic status of the child of zina (walad al-zina), permitting their purchase, enslavement, and sale, while explicitly excluding the foundling (laqit) from this category. This distinction highlights the specific legal treatment of bastards in early Shia fiqh, differentiating them from foundlings who were generally not subject to the same transactional rules. The hadith underscores the practical application of lineage and ownership rights in the context of the slave economy of the time.
